0968fa2631: I use Hermes with the NVIDIA provider (NVIDIA NIM, model moonshotai/kimi-k3) and a tool that returns a screenshot (computer use). The next model request fails with: `HTTP 400: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: data did not match any variant of untagged enum ChatCompletionRequestToolMessageContent at line 1 column 1974809`. Hermes treats this as a permanent request error, so every retry sends the same image-bearing tool result and fails the same way for the rest of the session. When Xiaomi MiMo, Alibaba or OpenCode Go reject image content inside tool results, Hermes recognises it, turns the tool result into text, remembers that provider/model, and retries; NVIDIA's wording should get the same recovery. Other NIM deserialization errors that are not about tool message content should still be treated as ordinary request errors.
28e6496a5e: Deleting a session from the web dashboard (the per-session DELETE call the UI makes) removes it from the database, but its files stay on disk in the profile's transcript folder: the `<id>.jsonl` transcript, the gateway's `request_dump_<id>_*.json` dumps, and the older-format `session_<id>.json` snapshot, which can contain plaintext secrets. It happens for the default profile and for a named profile selected with `?profile=<name>`. Deleting from the CLI does remove the transcript and the dumps, but even there (and when pruning old conversations) a legacy `session_<id>.json` snapshot is left behind. Deleting a session should remove all of its on-disk files, in the profile it belongs to, without touching another session's files (for example one whose id merely starts with the same text).
859b999db5: With an external memory provider configured, I send /new in a messaging chat (e.g. Telegram) through the gateway. The provider's end-of-session extraction for the old conversation is slow, so /new stops waiting for its cleanup after its timeout (30 s), and the cached agent for that chat is then evicted. The eviction shuts the memory provider down while the extraction is still running against it, and when the extraction finally finishes the provider is shut down a second time. Expected: while an end-of-session cleanup is still in progress, eviction should leave the shutdown to it, so the extraction completes against a live provider and the provider is shut down exactly once, afterwards.
e9eba2188a: I run `hermes dashboard` as its own process while a gateway is serving the same Hermes home, so the dashboard forwards session edits such as archiving (`PATCH /api/sessions/{id}`) to that gateway. When the gateway can't be reached at that moment, the errors are inconsistent: if the gateway has just died and its port refuses the WebSocket connection, the dashboard answers 409 ('Gateway connection failed; no local fallback'); if the gateway restarted between the dashboard finding it and asking it for a ticket, the answer is a 400. Only a raw socket error gives the retryable `503 owner_unreachable`. The UI treats 409 and 400 as final, so the edit is lost instead of retried. Any failure to reach the gateway should come back as 503 `owner_unreachable` (without the dashboard falling back to writing the database itself), while refusals the gateway actually sends back (permission_denied, not_found, storage_unavailable, ...) keep their current status codes.
652e4b9194: In the terminal UI (TUI), every time the agent of a live session is rebuilt (switching model mid-session with /model, resuming, or a late MCP refresh), one more background notification poller thread for that session is left running; a thread dump shows several `tui-notif-poller-<session id>` threads. The extra pollers keep consuming background-completion notifications and driving /loop, /heartbeat and bot delivery for that session, and closing the session only stops the newest one. After a rebuild there should be exactly one live notification poller per session, and the previous one should exit.
167a2d00ed: I archived one of my skills, later moved its folder out of `skills/.archive/` back into `skills/` by hand to use it again, and then archived it again with the manual archive subcommand. Minutes later, the `purge` subcommand that permanently deletes archived skills older than N days (`purge --days 30 --yes`) deleted it, even though it had only just been archived and its folder in `.archive/` was brand new. A skill should not be purged until it has really been archived for longer than the TTL. Archives made by older Hermes versions, whose folders still carry the skill's last-edit time, must still not be purged early either.
24b4f90e97: On native Windows with Python installed from the Microsoft Store, `hermes update` fails every Node build step with the refusal 'the command would start outside the update job', so the update can never finish its builds. Nothing is actually misbehaving: Store Python is a packaged interpreter, and a program it starts from outside its package (such as the managed node) is created outside the update's job because that job permits breakaway. The build should run, still contained by the update job; only a build command that Windows really will not place in the job should keep being refused without ever running.
3c53adbc1e: When I watch the agent's virtual desktop in the browser viewer (noVNC through Hermes's WebSocket bridge), the connection drops as soon as the viewer asks to resize the remote screen to fit its pane, which it does because Xvnc is started with `-AcceptSetDesktopSize`. The log shows `unknown RFB client message type 251` and the stream closes; the viewer reconnects and the same thing happens again. It happens whether or not the viewer holds the input lease. A resize request carries no input, so it should be passed through to Xvnc intact for every viewer, including when it arrives split across several WebSocket messages.
